summary.intent: Continue optimizing Callisto's release dry-run performance and robustness: after landing the git-process reduction in PR #365, address slow behavior under bad network conditions (offline/failing registry) and investigate Cargo lookup cost.
summary.outcome: Reduced the offline release dry-run from ~61 s to ~2.8 s by limiting failing-registry lookups to one retry, added a test pinning exactly two lookups (first try plus one retry), fixed a test that silently depended on real network, and ran full CI, adding a changeset and extending the stack. Reading the crates.io sparse index directly was deferred pending a trade-off write-up.

repo: Architecture rule: all VCS reads go through `GitAccess`; the git batching in #365 preserves it by reusing primitives that `status` and the changed-package check already use.
PRs are managed as native stacks (#364 -> #365 -> new patience PR); when a new fix touches a function rewritten by a lower PR, base it on the stack top rather than main.
`just ci` is the full local CI gate; changesets are added per PR.
npm and PyPI multi-package dry-run previews are fast (~0.9 s and ~0.7 s for 10 packages); Cargo is the slow ecosystem due to ~100 ms `cargo info` lookups per package.
Trusted mode legitimately probes that `cargo` exists, so test runners must only block the network lookup, not all cargo invocations.
A registry lookup for an unpublished crate is simulated in tests with exit code 101 and a `could not find` message.

code.finding: Holds the advisory/registry lookup check (including the `names_taken` context); modified so a failing registry gets at most one retry, which cut offline dry-run time from 61 s to 2.8 s. Line numbers not given in transcript.
Contains the local-release test setup reused for the new patience test asserting exactly two registry lookups and that the plan is still produced. Line numbers not given in transcript.

workflow: Measure real-world scenarios (offline, multi-package) with throwaway scripts in /tmp to find hidden slowness before optimizing.
Prefer deterministic process counts over wall-clock when network timing is noisy.
Write a design trade-off note before changes that alter authentication or trusted tooling, rather than just implementing them.
Tests that pass only because the real network answers a certain way are hidden dependencies; make fakes explicit.

friction: Wall-clock timing is noisy because crates.io `cargo info` calls are slow and variable.
The offline dry-run took ~61 s before the fix due to repeated registry retries.
Unit tests using git-only RealGitRunner failed after blocking network lookups: trusted mode's cargo-existence probe was blocked, and one test relied on the real network returning 'not found'.
The new fix touched a function rewritten by #364, requiring a rebase onto the stack top.
open_items: Cargo lookup cost (~100 ms per package) remains the main per-package cost; reading the crates.io sparse index directly for public crates is proposed but needs a trade-off write-up on authentication and which tool is trusted.
Remaining ~33 git processes per 10-crate preview: one parallel `git log` per package plus fixed costs.
Release PR #349 remains open alongside the stack.
